messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 1796543210 — High paging + continuous-batching anomaly detected in us-west1-prod. Alerts: cache_eviction_rate, streaming_token_cadence_stall, backend_5xx_increase. Severity: P1 (investigating).

maria (oncall-sre): I'm taking this. I see eviction rate spike ~12x starting 23:04 UTC, KV cache size jumped from 120GB -> 430GB over 8 minutes. Streaming nodes showing token cadence stalls and partial-flush timeouts.

raj (eng-runtime): we pushed a runtime tweak in last deploy (2026-03-14T22:50Z) that raised continuous_batch.max_tokens from 512 -> 2048 to optimize throughput for long-chat workloads. Hypothesis: large batch tokens + variable seq lengths cause cache-key fanout and thrash paging under heavy concurrency.

josh (support): Customer telemetry: two mid-market customers (acct: voyager-saas, acct: noteflow) reported increased dropped streaming responses and higher tail latency ~23:07 UTC. They saw sporadic 502/504 and stalled chunks. Logging shows partial flushes never completed; clients eventually time out.

elena (sre): I spun up additional cache replicas to buy time but eviction continues. Paging IOPS are at BL3 (saturation). Need an immediate config rollback or traffic-level throttle.

maria (oncall-sre): Agreed. Two-pronged mitigation: 1) hotfix config to cap continuous_batch.max_tokens=512 and continuous_batch.max_concurrent_batches=6; 2) enable prefix KV warmup (best-effort) and apply temporary rate-limit per-tenant for streaming routes that hit high page faults. Applying 1 now to a canary subset (us-west1-a).

raj (eng-runtime): ACK. Preparing a quick hotpatch. Patch snippet:

```yaml
# hotpatch - runtime continuous batching limiter
continuous_batch:
  max_tokens: 512
  max_concurrent_batches: 6
  prefix_caching: true
```

Command to push to canary pool: `./deploy-tools hotpatch --env=us-west1-a --patch=continuous_batch_limit.yaml`

maria (oncall-sre): Pushing now. Rolling canary to 10% of routers in us-west1-a. Will watch eviction rate and streaming cadence.

(2 minutes later)

maria (oncall-sre): Canary applied. Eviction rate down ~70% in canary hosts, paging IOPS reduced ~55%. Streaming token cadence in canary recovered to normal within one minute (:thumbsup:).

josh (support): Noted — reaching out to Voyager & Noteflow to let them know we have a partial mitigation and that we're rolling more broadly.

raj (eng-runtime): I'll prepare full-region rollout if canary remains stable for 5 more minutes. Also adding a guard in the config validation to prevent future deploys raising max_tokens above 1024 without an explicit opt-in.

elena (sre): Suggest also adding a metric alert for cache_growth_rate > 5x over 5m tied to an autoscale rollback playbook. Current alert thresholds were too loose for this pattern.

luke (pm): Please include customer impact details for the postmortem: which tenants were affected, duration, and what queries triggered the worst behavior. We should decide if credits or SLA gestures are needed.

maria (oncall-sre): Current impact table (first pass):
- voyager-saas: intermittent streaming stalls 23:07–23:21 UTC, ~3% of requests experienced partial flush/times out, support ticket open #INC-9873.
- noteflow: increased fail rate 23:06–23:18 UTC, ~2.2% error rate spike, digest logs attached.
- internal canary apps: degraded but recovered when canary hotpatch applied.

maria (oncall-sre): Broad rollout started at 23:15 UTC to remaining us-west1 pools. Monitoring.

(8 minutes later)

maria (oncall-sre): Full region rollout complete at 23:23 UTC. Eviction rate back to baseline within 3 minutes post-rollout. Streaming 95/99/Max tails improved; 5xx count trending down.

josh (support): I informed Voyager & Noteflow that we mitigated and are doing a root-cause follow-up. They asked for a rough ETA on a permanent fix.

raj (eng-runtime): Root cause plan: revert overly permissive batch defaults in runtime, add deployment validation gate, and add KV cache bloom filter tuning + prefetch heuristics to reduce paging on long-tail keys. We'll scope an RFC for the permanent changes.

elena (sre): Follow-ups for infra: add paging saturation alert, tighten LRU thresholds, and run a chaos test to validate continuous-batching increases under load.

maria (oncall-sre): Customer impact assessment: Severity P1 -> mitigated; impact window ~23:06–23:23 UTC, primary impact on streaming responses for specific tenants with long-chat profiles. Recommend SLA credit review and customer outreach draft.

oncall-night-bot: Handoff: maria -> night oncall (elena) at 23:45 UTC. Please monitor paging and streaming cadence for next 4 hours. Handoff notes attached in thread.

maria (oncall-sre): Handoff ack. I'll open the postmortem draft, include timeline, RCA hypothesis (batch_config_regression + kv_cache_paging_fanout), mitigation steps, and next actions. Assigning owners: raj (runtime fixes), elena (infra alerts + chaos), josh (customer comms). Anything else?

luke (pm): Add a short comms blurb for affected customers and a follow-up cadence for status. Good job on the rapid canary -> region rollout.

maria (oncall-sre): Thanks everyone. Closing incident as mitigated; will keep this thread updated with postmortem link and follow-ups.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1796543210 — Status changed: mitigated -> monitoring.
